newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. firms' letters of intent in Cuba out of date.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firms' letters of intent in Cuba out of date.

text.p: Letters of intent signed by U.S. firms interested in doing business in Cuba in the event the U.S. embargo is lifted are now out of date, a senior Cuban official said in remarks published on Tuesday.

Foreign Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradaz, interviewed by the Cuban business newspaper Negocios, said there had been a number of such letters. But these letters had a six-month expiry date that had now passed.

Ferradaz said it would have been impossible to sign letters of intent for an indefinite period, as this would have left Cuba's hands tied. He did not give the number of letters, or say in what sectors of investment they had involved.

Prior to March this year, when President Bill Clinton approved new legislation adding to the longstanding U.S. embargo, some U.S. firms appeared interested in positioning themselves for what they saw as a possible move by the U.S. administration to lift the 34-year trade ban soon.
But the new Helms-Burton law aims to broaden the embargo by, among other aspects, discouraging investment by third country firms.
